title: HVAA protection · mission sequence
subtitle: 2024 TTX · pulse support, ambush alert, decoy lines of effort
description: Mitchell Institute HVAA protection TTX team planned three distinct lines of effort to protect E-7A and tanker aircraft from long-range counterair threats (Figures 6–8, pp. 19–20).
assumptions: Figures 6–8 are notional planning diagrams rather than timestamped real aircraft tracks.
The team envisioned first-day F-15EX air launches and subsequent ground launches from the Ryukyus for some recoverable EW CCA, but no precise coordinates or per-flight headings were published.
The report described up to four reactive waves per day depending on target availability; current timeline seconds and moving actors are illustrative.
Displayed threat relationships do not establish real sensor connectivity, kill chains or engagement results.

phases.title: LOE 1 · HVAA pulse support
phases.narrative: CCA and F-22s were proposed to counter KJ-500 and airborne threats to E-7A and tankers during strikes.

phases.title: LOE 2 · Ambush alert
phases.narrative: Reactive expendable air-to-air CCA supported by recoverable EW/ISR CCA would maintain pressure between strikes.

phases.title: LOE 3 · Decoy operations
phases.narrative: Recoverable EW and ISR CCA were intended to compel PLA defensive responses and identify targets of opportunity.

phases.title: LOEs recur intermittently
phases.narrative: Cycle reset visualizes concurrent and repeated concepts, not actual sortie timing.
